correspondence.finding: The southern piece approaches northeastward from the Wilhelmina–De Kock mountain setting into the upper Saramacca corridor. Holthuis's map depicts this southern approach separately from the western Toekoemoetoe creek branch. Its generalized mountain-side ending does not establish a name for the model's first small feeder.

The selected route continues north and then bends east around the Jan Basi Gado setting before resuming northward. That distinctive middle bend appears on the historical map's Saramacca River corridor; the selection does not turn west into the separately drawn Coppename drainage.

The northward middle trunk stays west of the Brokopondo waterbody and Suriname River. The retained 2003 institutional map labels Saramacca R. in this corridor and distinguishes the neighboring rivers; the selected route contains no Brokopondo reservoir passage.

The lower route matches the ministry's mapped sequence through the Pikin Saron bridge setting, Uitkijk, Groningen and the Saramacca bridge, then west across the coastal plain. The report explicitly identifies these locations with the Saramacca River and describes tidal influence in its estuary.

The westward final piece reaches the Saramacca–Coppename confluence setting shown on both lower-course maps. The selection ends there rather than continuing north along the common estuarine approach to the Atlantic; its endpoint is not asserted to be a surveyed mouth or exact confluence vertex.
The selected western beginning approaches Uauá from the southwest and continues east. INEMA labels this upper corridor Rio Vaza-Barris, separately mapping Riacho da Besta, Riachão and Alagoinha.
The route crosses the Cocorobó reservoir setting by Canudos. INEMA distinguishes the southern Bendengó contribution from the selected western Vaza-Barris approach.
Beyond Canudos the selection follows the eastward corridor past Jeremoabo, then bends south through the Coronel João Sá setting toward Sergipe.
IBGE labels the continuing river Vaza-Barris inside Sergipe, with Salgado, Lombada and Traíras entering the corridor; the separate Sergipe and Poxim networks lie to its northeast.

The selected southeastward ending reaches the branching lower estuarine setting near Ilha Grande. IBGE maps its Atlantic outlet context at Barra de São Cristóvão; no exact selected mouth channel is assigned.

correspondence.scope: Initial northern loop, Bear Lakes and West Aishihik approach
correspondence.finding: The detailed East Kluane sheet locates the modeled beginning near the Twelfth of July Creek terrain. Its ensuing northward and eastward loop follows the vicinity of a subzone boundary toward Bear Lakes, rather than a clearly demonstrated continuous mapped watercourse. That first connection remains unresolved. Farther east and south, the selected line corresponds to the Bear Lakes chain and the labeled West Aishihik River. The separate federal fisheries map distinguishes this western river from Sekulmun, Aishihik and Canyon Lakes; those larger lakes cannot be substituted for the actual selected upstream line.

correspondence.scope: Lower Aishihik and Dezadeash approach to Alsek
correspondence.finding: After the southeastward West Aishihik reach, the selection turns south along lower Aishihik River and then west on Dezadeash River past the Haines Junction setting. The Yukon map depicts those named receiving corridors, and the federal station index independently nests West Aishihik under Aishihik, Aishihik under Dezadeash, and Dezadeash under Alsek. The Parks Canada map separately shows the Kaskawulsh River arriving from western glacier country. Neither the Kaskawulsh arm nor the eastern Dezadeash Lake source arm is included merely because it contributes water to the selected downstream route.

correspondence.scope: Alsek trunk through the Yukon and British Columbia glacier corridor
correspondence.finding: The two middle mainstem pieces continue south along the mapped Alsek corridor, pass through the Lowell Lake setting beside Lowell Glacier, cross the Yukon–British Columbia boundary and continue beside the Tweedsmuir Glacier setting toward the Tatshenshini junction. Parks Canada and BC Parks depict the same connected valley sequence. Lowell, Dusty and other glacier-fed side drainages are distinct contributors; the selection is not a centerline through their glacier interiors. Lake passage and adjacent river reaches are kept distinct, and no exact present glacier front or hydronym-transition vertex is assigned.

correspondence.scope: Three selected pieces of the Tatshenshini branch
correspondence.finding: The three gray pieces form one connected eastern branch: southward from below the Dalton Post setting, then southwest and west into the Alsek junction. This is the corridor separately labeled Tatshenshini River on the park maps. The selected branch does not include the whole upper Tatshenshini or its source region, and its three modeled pieces are not three independently established tributary names.

correspondence.scope: Lower Alsek, Alsek Lake and Dry Bay
correspondence.finding: Below the Tatshenshini junction the selected mainstem continues southwest, turns south through the Alsek Lake setting and then west toward Dry Bay. The NPS map and accompanying description distinguish the Alsek River and lake from East Alsek River, Grand Plateau Lake and the glacier-separated possible future outlet. The modeled terminal route corresponds to the Dry Bay side, not the illustrated future Grand Plateau route. The selected endpoint is not certified as a surveyed river mouth, tidal boundary or complete coastal channel.

correspondence: Both selected mainstem fragments were inspected. The route runs southwest from the northern interior, turns broadly east, then bends southeast and ends after a short eastward lower section. No separate tributary fragment is selected.

The long northern and middle legs lie within the mapped Inland Ice. The southeastward lower continuation approaches the glaciated southeastern margin. The source graticule, ice contours and adjoining coastal land arrangement support this regional feature-class reading, without assigning the line to a specific glacier, fjord or marginal stream.

The readable source does not establish a natural river hydronym for the whole modeled route. Regional glacier, coastal-land or fjord labels cannot be transferred onto a continuous modeled inland river line. This hold does not assert that every small marginal waterway is unnamed.

The legend distinguishes ice-surface contours, dashed ice-thickness isopachs, sub-ice bedrock contours and aeromagnetic lineaments south of 68°N. None of these cartographic lines establishes a named river or proves present-day surface or subglacial connectivity along the selected path.

scope_limit: MAIN_RIV groups and model mainstem roles do not establish a uniform name for every included reach, tributary or lake passage. Source observations support only the stated representative identity or hold.
publication_boundary: Own factual observations, attribution and official public URLs only; source originals, images, complete coordinates and private evidence remain omitted.
